purpose: PET4D provides a DICOM plugin for loading ECG-gated, dynamic, and static PET series into 3D Slicer as volume sequences with SUV (bw/lbm/bsa) or Bq/ml scaling, decay correction, and frame timing metadata. It also provides interactive modules for frame-by-frame review/editing, motion correction, PET-to-CT/MR registration, and compartmental/graphical kinetic modeling (1TC, 2TC, Patlak, Logan, SRTM, SUVR) for nuclear medicine researchers.
summary:
PET4D is a well-engineered, self-contained 3D Slicer extension for loading, reviewing, motion-correcting, registering, and kinetically modeling gated and dynamic PET series. It relies solely on Slicer-bundled Python packages (`numpy`, `scipy`, `SimpleITK`, `pydicom`) and built-in CLI modules (`BRAINSFit`, `BRAINSResample`), has no network activity or unsafe operations, is released under the MIT license, and has valid CMake packaging and thorough tests.

🟢 Recommend merge

safety.rationale: Searched and inspected the codebase for network calls, subprocess execution, dynamic code execution, file deletion, and deserialization. The extension operates entirely locally on user-selected MRML nodes, DICOM database series, and user-chosen CSV paths, using `tempfile.mkdtemp` cleanly for temporary DICOM export staging and unit tests.

environment.rationale: Inspected all Python files and imports across `DICOMGatedDynamicPET/` and `DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib/`. The extension uses only standard library modules and packages already bundled with Slicer (`numpy`, `scipy`, `SimpleITK`, `pydicom`, `vtk`, `qt`, `ctk`, `slicer`), performs no `pip_install` calls, and does not modify global Slicer or Python settings on import.

packaging.rationale: Inspected `CMakeLists.txt`, `DICOMGatedDynamicPET/CMakeLists.txt`, and `PET4D.json`. All 6 scripted modules (`DICOMGatedDynamicPET`, `GatedDynamicPETSettings`, `DynamicPETEditor`, `DynamicPETMotionCorrection`, `DynamicPETRegistration`, `DynamicPETModeling`), all 19 library files under `DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib/`, and all referenced icons and images exist and are properly listed in `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` calls. (The automated heuristic note about uninstalled Python files is a false positive because those modules are built via subsequent `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule` calls in `DICOMGatedDynamicPET/CMakeLists.txt`.)

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE`, which provides a standard permissive MIT License (Copyright (c) 2026 Burak Demir), and verified that no third-party binaries, restricted weights, or incompatible code are bundled.

soundness.rationale: Inspected the module classes, DICOM plugin implementation, and library modules (`petseries.py`, `kinetics.py`, `dicomexport.py`, etc.). Modules follow Slicer conventions (`ScriptedLoadableModule`, `VTKObservationMixin`, proper observer and temporary helper node cleanup on exit/scene close, progress dialogs with cancellation support), and algorithmic logic is cleanly separated into a testable Slicer-independent library with comprehensive unit and module tests.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md`, module help texts, and `Testing/`. The extension addresses a clear gap in Slicer for 4D (dynamic and ECG-gated) PET loading, frame editing, motion correction, registration, and kinetic modeling, includes a prominent research-only clinical disclaimer in `README.md`, and provides extensive documentation and unit tests.

findings.title: Catalog entry PET4D.json committed in extension source repository
findings.explanation: The catalog entry file `PET4D.json` belongs in the Slicer Extensions Index repository rather than inside the extension's own source repository. It is harmless, but unnecessary in the source repository.
findings.suggestion: Optionally remove `PET4D.json` from the extension source repository, as the catalog entry is maintained in `Slicer/ExtensionsIndex`.
